clean: Journal entry. Today was Dad's 70th birthday and we finally did the boat trip he's been talking about for years. It rained the whole morning and I was sure he'd be disappointed, but he spent three hours on deck in a borrowed raincoat telling the skipper about the boats he used to fix in the eighties. My brother Cormac flew in from Edmonton, he moved last spring and I keep forgetting, and it was the first time the three of us had been in one place since Mom's funeral. Nobody said anything about that, which I think was right. At dinner Dad made a little speech and said he was proud of us, which he has never once said out loud, and I had to leave the table for a minute. I want to remember how he looked when the sun finally came out around 4.

clean: This section explains how we triage incoming auto claims during storm events. When the volume goes above roughly 300 new claims a day, the intake team switches to the surge workflow, which means that every claim gets a severity score at first notice of loss instead of waiting for an adjuster. Scores of 1 and 2 are cosmetic damage and can be handled through the photo estimating app without an inspection. Scores of 3 and above go to a field adjuster, and anything involving an injury goes straight to the bodily injury unit regardless of the score. The point is not to process faster for its own sake, it's to make sure the people with undrivable cars or injuries hear from us within 48 hours, 24 was the old target and we never hit it. Loucaster's team owns the scoring rubric and reviews it after every event.
